sentence_stem: Having finished the report by noon,
correct_completion: she was finally able to take a break.
full_sentence: Having finished the report by noon, she was finally able to take a break.
acceptable_variants: she finally had time to rest.
she could relax for the first time that week.

options.text: she will finish the report by noon.
options.why_wrong: The perfect participle 'having finished' already places the completion before the main clause, so repeating the deadline as a future action contradicts the stem.

options.text: she had been dreading the meeting all morning.
options.why_wrong: This describes a feeling, not a result of completing the report, so it breaks the logical link the participle clause sets up.

options.text: she was finally able to take a break.
the report was still on her desk.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts the stem, which states that the report is already finished.

grammar_focus: Perfect participle clauses expressing a completed action before the main clause
explanation: The perfect participle 'having finished' shows that the action in the first clause is completed before the action in the main clause. The main clause must therefore describe a logical result of that completion. Learners whose first language expresses this sequence with a separate time-ordered sentence may find the compressed participle form less natural at first, so comparing the two structures helps.
translation: Закінчивши звіт до полудня, вона нарешті змогла відпочити.
